value.text:
Claude Bernard University Lyon 1, also known as Lyon 1, is a public university in the Lyon area of France. The institution uses the French name Université Claude-Bernard-Lyon-I and announced the Lyon 1 Université Claude Bernard brand in January 2026. It concentrates on science and technology, health disciplines, and sports science. Its administrative and teaching facilities extend beyond a single site: the LyonTech-la Doua campus in Villeurbanne houses headquarters and science and sport faculties, while Lyon Health East Campus serves medical and dental education and research.

Lyon's Faculty of Science arose from an 1808 decree, and a medical and pharmacy faculty was founded in 1874. Those earlier faculties should be distinguished from the present university, formed through their consolidation under a decree dated 8 December 1970; some accounts describe the institutional establishment as 1971. The university subsequently developed an extensive set of facilities across the metropolitan area, including medical sites and an observatory. It has been associated with successive University of Lyon groupings, which are distinct from Lyon 1 itself.

Its teaching covers biology, chemistry, mathematics, computing and engineering alongside medicine, pharmacy, dentistry, allied health and sport. The French-language article describes six teaching and research faculties, three institutes, four schools and three independent departments. Its 2023 information reports roughly 46,000–47,000 students and a budget of €480 million; a later narrative gives a €519 million budget for 2025. These dated figures should not be read as simultaneous or directly comparable current totals.
